When the input-to-output edge 3 is absent, deleting edge 4 removes one of the few remaining paths into the output (exp 42, 44 vs 41, 43).
Without edge 3, edge 5 carries a larger share of the signal into the output, and it can reconnect a cell whose output was cut off (exp 17 vs 11-16, 18-20).
Adding a conv on edge 4 matters much more when the direct edge 3 is missing, since it may be the only output path (exp 93 vs 91, 95, 96).
Skip-dominated cells lack learnable capacity, so adding a 3x3 conv to them yields large gains, whereas conv-rich cells barely improve (exp 28, 29 vs 21-27).
Inserting a conv into a parameter-free all-skip cell gives a huge improvement compared with conv-rich parents (exp 85 vs 11-20).
Replacing edge 1's conv with pooling is nearly harmless when edge 0 still provides a conv, but catastrophic when it removes the only conv in a skip or pool cell (exp 51-53, 56-58, 60 vs 54, 59).
Adding another 3x3 conv shows diminishing returns in cells already containing 3x3 convs, versus large gains in skip or 1x1 cells (exp 61-67, 70 vs 68, 69).
Deleting edge 4 hurts more when it removes a 3x3 conv than when it removes a skip, pool or 1x1 op (exp 41-45, 49, 50 vs 46-48).
